name: PTOLEMY
full_name: Princeton Tritium Observatory for Light, Early-Universe, Massive-Neutrino Yield
summary: PTOLEMY is a research programme aimed at detecting the cosmic neutrino background through neutrino capture on tritium. It also develops precision beta spectroscopy and tritium-target technologies.
detection_principle: Relic electron neutrinos could be captured on tritium without an energy threshold, producing electrons just above the beta endpoint. A thin tritium target, precision filtering and calorimetry must separate these electrons from the much larger beta spectrum.

sites.name: International project; prototype R&D at Gran Sasso, Italy, and elsewhere, with the final full-array site undecided
sites.location: International project; prototype R&D at Gran Sasso, Italy, and elsewhere, with the final full-array site undecided

status.label: Research and development
status.evidence: The LNGS demonstrator is being assembled to test tritium sources, electromagnetic filtering and radio-frequency preselection. Full relic-neutrino detection remains a long-term objective.

collaboration.name: PTOLEMY Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Signal signature
key_parameters.value: Electron energy above the ordinary beta endpoint

results.summary: The proposal describes the relic-neutrino capture concept and required detector developments.

science_scope: A relic-neutrino capture peak has not been detected. Target loading, energy resolution and backgrounds are central technical challenges; conceptual sensitivity should not be confused with a discovery or a measured cosmic-neutrino flux.
